items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I found that Mr. Ginley knew more about jazz and American artists than I did... And I had a most beautiful evening... with Booker T. Pitman. ... Mr. Ginley also showed me a book that he had written on Zsa Zsa Gabor.

ctx.x: Just sidetracking Texas for awhile, to -- to bring in Booker T. Pitman. I met Booker and we hugged each other because we hadn't seen each other in so many years. And Booker asked me to join them, they were going up to -- up to George E. Ginley's apartment. To hear some sounds, just like that. I said, okay. So we all got in cabs. And went up on the 25th floor at this penthouse of Mr. Ginley. And I found that Mr. Ginley knew more about jazz and American artists than I did. Because he had a blues room in his home,…

And I had a most beautiful evening, and a most beautiful stay in Rio, with Booker T. Pitman. I met his wife. She was a black woman, the color of my shoe, but a very smart person. And at this particular party there were people of color, from all over Brazil, business people. And they were all just like one big family. Mr. Ginley owned three or four magazines and he periodically would fly models in to appear in his magazines. So these ladies were flown out from California to appear in his magazines.
